title: The Translation lifecycle runs itself
description:
A published Story in a site with other languages needs a translation per language: wanted, translating, held (a quotation or a check needs a person), ready, published, stale (the source changed). A new source version marks affected blocks stale and wakes the translator for those blocks only; blocks a person corrected are pinned and never overwritten. A held translation raises one flag and waits; the others proceed.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every published Story has, per language, exactly one state.
- A source edit re-translates only what changed.
- A hold blocks one translation, never the queue.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- translation-lifecycle.feature: a publish wants one translation per language; an edit marks only changed blocks stale; a pinned block survives; a hold flags once and others proceed.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Lifecycles that run themselves: Reference, Idea, Translation, Illustration. Slice code K3 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.

comments.text: Closing 2026-11-23 after an audit of develop and main: shipped and released in #1726. One state per language and a hold that blocks only its own translation (translation-lifecycle.feature); a source edit marks it stale and only what changed is translated again, keeping a person's wording (story-localize.feature 'Only what changed is translated again', translation-correction.feature).
